builds.howItPlays: You play cheap units like Clockwork Keeper, a 2-cost unit that draws you a card if you pay one extra Calm rune, and spend the extra rune Ornn gives you each turn, which only pays for gear, on cheap gear that readies Pit Crew so it can attack again. Then you put Sterak's Gage, which attaches the moment you play it and gives +3 Might, on one attacker to win fights and conquer battlefields early.
builds.whyYou: You like getting units down in the first turns and making your opponent deal with them before their own plan starts. You enjoy the small puzzle each turn asks: which cheap gear to play with Ornn's extra rune, when to ready Pit Crew, which attacker gets Sterak's Gage. Your units start small, but a steady stream of gear keeps them growing and your hand full enough to keep attacking. If winning fast by stacking small advantages on a busy board sounds fun, this Ornn suits you.

builds.howItPlays: You protect a few big units with Zhonya's Hourglass, a 2-cost gear you hide face down that sends your unit back to base instead of letting it die, and Not So Fast, which counters an enemy spell or ability aimed at your units or gear. Then you play 6-cost Ornn, Forge God or Azir, Ascendant, load them with Svellsongur (which copies the text of the unit it's attached to) and World Atlas, and score points by holding battlefields turn after turn.
builds.whyYou: You'd rather build one fortress than race your opponent. You like drawing extra cards, keeping an answer ready for their turn, and watching a single unit grow bigger with every gear you stack on it. Games run long and you're fine with that, because once your biggest unit is loaded with gear and protected, your opponent has to spend turn after turn trying to shift it. If a slow, careful game that ends with one unit nobody can remove sounds fun, this Ornn suits you.
